recap: Goal: the Future War look of The Terminator (1984). Compare the original game, selected V2 references and five new Mac captures below.
Kite3D 0.19.0-alpha.2 now shares identical texture sources, loads exact baked atmosphere pixels and overlaps shader preparation. V2 appearance, gameplay and enemy overlay removal remain.
Isolated Mac: 75.84 FPS over 60 seconds of native combat with 24 actors, High, actual 1512×982 buffer; prior PR: 78.41 FPS. This is no steady-frame guarantee.
Actual Play click to ready: cold 8.33 seconds, warm 7.31; manager restart 5.70. Earlier totals included automation before the click. Art refinement remains deferred to issue #2.

performance_notes: Images are the five original, unedited 1920×1080 POVs from Mac capture set 22, source 927fc43fa0ee864752cfb1a5ac2dde6feaefdef2. The parent verified all 136 runtime source hashes and all five PNG hashes; the export binds those results to the complete capture manifest. These fixed tick-120 images are visual evidence, not populated FPS measurements. Camera, feet, support, map state and weapon match the original saved captures exactly.

The captured loading work is integrated in private PR revision 5001f0a. It includes exact noise baking, identical image Source sharing and shader preparation overlap. The experimental direct-Blob bitmap loader is not part of this milestone.

Latest isolated native 60-second combat: candidate 75.84 FPS versus unchanged prior PR 78.41 FPS, CPU medians 10.2 and 10.4 ms respectively. The candidate CPU p95 is 14.2 ms and frame-cadence p95 is 23.9 ms. This uses the High preset’s actual 1512×982 drawing buffer on the M3 Max; it is neither 1920×1080 capture timing nor physical 3024×1964 Retina timing. An average over 75 FPS does not establish a sustained 13.33 ms frame budget or guarantee steady frames.

Earlier 90.9 FPS came from a separate headed run under different conditions. Later 42–60 FPS runs, including an unchanged control, were affected by duplicate-editor and desktop interference; isolating the owned test restored both control and candidate above 75 FPS on average. Those runs remain historical context rather than a single comparable performance series. No unrelated applications were modified.

Measurement correction: the earlier 14.96 s and 11.69 s totals began before Playwright waited for the Play button to become actionable. They included waiting before the actual click and must not be labeled button-press loading time. New run 25 records the real DOM click event: cold 8.3321 s, warm 7.3062 s, manager restart 5.6956 s to the ready gate. Its corresponding automation-intent totals are 11.9447, 10.8768 and 5.6956 s, including 3.6126, 3.5706 and 0 s before start. This is a corrected measurement boundary, not an additional optimization or time manually subtracted from an old run. The actual-click cold and warm ready gates are under 10 seconds in these measurements.

Run 25 used b49b22722b71dfd97447064797d88f7bd6beb6f6, whose runtime is parent-verified identical to the integrated private revision 5001f0a; only diagnostic timing code differs. There is no bitmap pilot. The editor startup buffer was 1017×926. Input followed the cold ready gate by 7.8 ms; the subsequent 7.5 m movement / 97-tick proof completed 9.9892 s after the real click. Cold/warm/restart are separate cases with no synthetic three-second dwell. Four actor visuals were present, but this run’s new enemy draw observer recorded no IDs, so it is not proof of four actors drawn. Prior readiness check 13 and populated native combat provide separate rendering evidence; this diagnostic gap remains explicit. Page errors were empty, but each case retains a console connection-refused entry and two failed /api/lobby requests; cold and warm also record two aborted blob requests. These are preserved as network/console limitations, not reported as zero errors.

Validation: 435 Node tests passed, with 11 skips. Google Chrome with Metal check 21 passed Playable, Editable and Persisted. The earlier default bundled-headless check failed its 30-frame watchdog and is retained as a separate failed configuration, not erased by the successful Chrome/Metal result. Readiness check 13 passed all cycles and first-use texture/program residency checks. Visual check 14 and the new five-view set 22 were reviewed without appearance regressions.

All 18 previous milestones and all seven original user quotations are preserved. Linux timings in earlier archives remain provisional because accidental external editor tabs could not be safely closed. No Mac acceptance is inferred from Linux, and no new GPU measurements were made while building this gallery.
